sentences.text:
T.N.Dubey vs Dr. I.D.Kalwani Deceased Through Lrs. on 21 July,
2023
Bench: Hrishikesh Roy, Pankaj Mithal
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Miscellaneous Application No. 1561 Of 2023
 In
 Criminal Appeal No. 1188/2011
 T.N. Dubey & Anr. Applica
 Versus
 Dr. I.D. Kalwani Deceased Through Lrs. Non-App
 W I T H
 Criminal Appeal No. 1188 Of 2011
 (Taken On Board)
 O R D E R
Miscellaneous Application No. 1561 of 2023 in Criminal Appeal No. 1188 of 2011 Delay in filing
restoration application is condoned.

Heard Mr. Siddharth Dubey, learned counsel appearing for the
applica
nts. Also heard Mr. B.S. Rajesh Agrajit, learned counsel appearing for the non-applicant(s).
Heard and considered the plea of the parties on the application for restoration.
I.A. No. 129593 of 2023 for restoration is allowed.
Criminal Appeal is restored to its original number.
Miscellaneous Application is accordingly disposed of.

Criminal Appeal No. 1188 of 2011 Heard learned counsel for the parties on the merits of the criminal appeal which came to be dismissed on 22.02.2023 for want of prosecution from the side of the appellants.

The order passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bilaspur in Complaint Case No. 123 of 2010 is noticed together with the fact that the handwriting expert had given adverse (forged) opinion on the signature in the concerned document.

On this basis, direction was issued for taking cognizance of offence under Sections 420,
467, 468 and 469/34 of IPC against the accused.
Considering the above, we see no infirmity with the order passed by the High Court on 07.05.2010 in Crl. M.P. No. 310 of 2010, refusing to quash the criminal process.
Consequently, the appeal stands dismissed.
..................J. (HRISHIKESH ROY) ..................J. (PANKAJ MITHAL) NEW DELHI;

Criminal Appeal is restored to its original number.
